intro: Editors manage deadlines, judge quality and guide writers, skills that media and marketing roles reward. The closest of the 25 careers below are Producers and Directors and Film and Video Editors, both at an 83% match; producers earn a BLS May 2025 median of $90,360, which is 16% more than the $77,920 editors earn.
why_it_works: Your days are spent deciding what works, cutting what does not and keeping a publishing schedule on track. O*NET rates time management at 3.38 out of 5 for editors and judgment at 3.25. Producing, art direction and advertising roles use the same editorial eye. All 25 matches need no new degree. The common gaps are coordination across teams, managing budgets and reading people.
tips: Build a portfolio that shows results, such as traffic, subscribers or awards, not only clean copy.
Art Directors are an 82% match and earn $114,850, which is 47% more.
Take on a campaign or video project at work to test producing before you switch.

faq.q: What jobs can former editors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Producers and Directors (83%), Film and Video Editors (83%) and Art Directors (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Film and Video Editors earn $75,420, which is 3% less than the $77,920 editor median, but use many of the same skills.

faq.q: Which careers for editors pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more than editing. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (114% more), Public Relations Managers $146,910 (89% more) and Advertising and Promotions Managers $133,660 (72% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These manager roles usually expect several years of experience.

faq.q: Do editors need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than editors already have. A bachelor's degree is the most common level, held by 57% of workers in the closest match, so a strong portfolio matters more than a new diploma.

The skills that most often need work are managing materials, coordination, systems evaluation and social perceptiveness. Complex problem solving already rates 3.25 out of 5 for editors in O*NET, so working across teams and budgets is the main step.
